**Opacity ($g_o$):** Defined as the occupancy output after the last upsampling layer of the network.
**Initializer Network ($\theta_I$):** Takes SfM points as input.
Uses sparse 3D convolutions in an encoder-decoder architecture.
Dense CNN blocks are used in the bottleneck followed by upsampling layers to increase voxel density.
**Densifier Network ($\theta_D$):** Predicts additional voxel features in free space.
**Optimizer Network ($\theta_O$):** Uses a sparse 3D UNet architecture.
Inputs are latent voxel features $G_t$ and their gradients $\nabla G_t$.
*   **Render and Gradient:** Render current Gaussians $G_t$ using all training images.
*   **Importance Sampling:** Select a subset of new Gaussians for densification.
Sample weighted by occupancy predictions of upsampled voxels (interpreted as opacity).
*   **Memory Complexity:** The method uses a sparse voxel grid.
QuickSplat was introduced by Yueh-Cheng Liu, Lukas Höllein, Matthias Nießner, and Angela Dai from the Technical University of Munich.

It builds on 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) [26] and integrates learned priors from data, similar to approaches like SGNN [15] and G3R [11], but applies them to Gaussian primitives for surface reconstruction.
It is evaluated on the ScanNet++ dataset [55], which contains 902 indoor scenes.
